"Pakistan imposes emergency rule in province governed by Imran Khan's party"
Standfirst: "PM's office says cabinet move follows 'provincial government's deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism'."
BYLINE: "By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters" - Reuters attribution. Photo credit: Abdul Majeed/AFP.

Pakistan announced a STATE OF EMERGENCY in the northwestern KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA province, invoked on SUNDAY under two articles of the constitution dealing with security. "It effectively suspends the provincial government run by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of jailed former Prime Minister IMRAN KHAN."
President ASIF ALI ZARDARI said in a social media post he had approved the recommendations made by the cabinet, which met under Prime Minister SHEHBAZ SHARIF earlier in the day.
Sharif's office statement: cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the "provincial government's deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism".
ARRESTS: Shortly after the announcement, PTI lawmaker JUNAID AKBAR said SOHAIL AFRIDI, the CHIEF MINISTER of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, was arrested along with the party's president in the province.
The provincial GOVERNOR will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister AZAM NAZEER TARAR told a news conference in Islamabad, adding the arrangement will initially be in place for SIX MONTHS.
PTI spokesperson and Khan aide ZULFIKAR BUKHARI described the move as "more of a coup disguised as emergency" and warned it would cause "further bloodshed, instability and collateral damage".
CONTEXT: comes as the PTI prepares a march on Islamabad demanding Khan's release. Khan has been in jail for MORE THAN THREE YEARS but "still commands widespread popularity across the country". The march was originally scheduled for 27 September, postponed to 4 October for talks. The government said it would not allow the march to enter the capital and has erected barriers using shipping containers to block main access routes.
